claims.text: The feedstock is a cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder intended for laser-based additive manufacturing.
In-situ substrate pre-heating during L-PBF will reduce the cooling rate of AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate pre-heating will reduce compositional segregation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate pre-heating will reduce residual thermal stresses in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate pre-heating will reduce defect formation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Pre-heating will produce a refined, more compositionally uniform AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Slower interlayer cooling reduces thermal gradients that cause segregation and stress accumulation.
Solidification-related mechanical solicitation and residual-stress distributions are associated with cracking in L-PBF high-entropy alloys.
Rapid non-equilibrium melting and solidification occur during laser processing of high-entropy alloys.
Room-temperature-substrate L-PBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces compositional inhomogeneity, high residual stress, and defects.
Pre-heated builds will have improved yield strength relative to room-temperature-substrate L-PBF builds.
Pre-heated builds will have improved ductility relative to room-temperature-substrate L-PBF builds.
The hypothesis is limited to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi processed by L-PBF and may not extend to other alloy systems or non-laser additive-manufacturing processes.
The optimal substrate pre-heating temperature may depend on the equipment and alloy.
Holding laser power, scan speed, atmosphere, and post-processing constant while varying substrate temperature provides a controlled test of the intervention.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in residual stress, segregation, and defect density, or failure to improve mechanical performance, would falsify the hypothesis.
